taxonomyNote: NatureServe (citing Nicholson 2025) recognizes three subspecies (Sierran, Western Red-tailed, and an unnamed Inyo skink); formerly in genus Eumeces.
fieldMarks: Smooth, shiny scales; olive to brown above, sometimes with dark patterning; up to about 4.5 inches.
Young have a brilliant blue or pink tail contrasting with the body.
behavior: Eats insects and spiders, searching under leaves and surface objects.
Lays 3-9 eggs in summer, in chambers in loose soil (peak activity around 1 July in one California account); not territorial.
Inactive in cold temperatures and extreme heat.
habitat: Varied: grassland, salt flats, high desert, open chaparral, pinyon-juniper and open pine forest, often rocky areas near streams and springs.
In California foothills up to about 1,980 m, favouring chaparral, black oak woodland and riparian deciduous habitat.
range: Sierra Nevada and Coast Ranges of California south to northern Baja California, with isolated populations in southeastern California, southern Nevada and west-central Arizona; sea level to about 2,200 m.
